parks.name: Everglades National Park — Ernest F. Coe Visitor Center
parks.hook: UNESCO World Heritage gate at Coe; then the Anhinga boardwalk four miles in through sawgrass.
parks.whyGo: Start at the main Homestead entrance when the day is about seeing the River of Grass, not just crossing it on the Tamiami Trail.
parks.knownFor: The Coe Visitor Center is the park's primary south entrance. Royal Palm and the Anhinga Trail sit a short drive inside the gate.
parks.funFact: Everglades National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site. NPS wet-season guidance (May–November) is to plan for heat and mosquitoes.

parks.name: Everglades National Park — Shark Valley
parks.hook: Heart of the freshwater marsh on a 15-mile loop; climb the 70-foot observation tower at the midpoint.
parks.whyGo: Choose Shark Valley when the Everglades need to be a loop you can bike or tram, not a boardwalk stop.
parks.knownFor: A paved 15-mile tram/bike loop through sawgrass marsh, with the observation tower at the halfway point.
parks.funFact: NPS lists the Shark Valley tower as the highest elevation a visitor can reach by foot in the park, at 70 feet, with views up to 20 miles.

parks.name: Biscayne National Park
parks.hook: A park that is 95 percent water; walk the Jetty boardwalk over Biscayne Bay from Convoy Point.
parks.whyGo: Come here when the national-park day should be the bay and the reef, not another trail through sawgrass.
parks.knownFor: Coral reefs, mangrove shoreline, Biscayne Bay, and 10,000 years of human history. Most of the park is on the water.
parks.funFact: The official NPS homepage states the park is 95% water. Guided eco-adventures leave from the Dante Fascell Visitor Center.

parks.name: Big Cypress National Preserve
parks.hook: America's first national preserve; stretch on the H.P. Williams boardwalk over the Tamiami cypress.
parks.whyGo: Stop on the Tamiami when the Everglades day needs cypress strand, not only open marsh.
parks.knownFor: Scenic drives, boardwalk talks, and eight campgrounds across the preserve.
parks.funFact: Big Cypress was designated the first national preserve in the U.S. National Park System. NPS lists discovery hikes, boardwalk talks, and interpretive canoe programs.

parks.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
parks.hook: America's first undersea park; swim the beach or start at the visitor-center aquariums in Key Largo.
parks.whyGo: Drive to Key Largo when the reef is the reason, and you want a state-park gate rather than a private boat-only day.
parks.knownFor: The first undersea park in the United States, protecting living coral reef off Key Largo.
parks.funFact: Florida State Parks identifies Pennekamp as America's first undersea park. The visitor-center aquariums are the landside start when you are not getting in the water.

parks.name: Bahia Honda State Park
parks.hook: Flagler's Old Bahia Honda Bridge as overlook; then the park's sandy beaches below.
parks.whyGo: Keep driving when the Keys day should end on sand you can walk, with the old railroad bridge as the overlook.
parks.knownFor: Beaches on a small Keys island and the remnant of Henry Flagler's Overseas Railroad bridge.
parks.funFact: The Old Bahia Honda Bridge is the park's landmark overlook; the beaches sit below the abandoned rail span.

parks.name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park
parks.hook: Southeast Florida's largest state park; hike Hobe Mountain, the ancient sand-dune overlook.
parks.whyGo: Head north when the drive should be pine flatwoods and a dune overlook, not another bay park.
parks.knownFor: The largest state park in Southeast Florida, with the Hobe Mountain observation point on an ancient sand dune.
parks.funFact: Florida State Parks identifies Jonathan Dickinson as Southeast Florida's largest state park. Hobe Mountain is the park's sand-dune overlook.
